previous_assumption: Assumed restricting the new RequirementService.updateRequirement to status === 'open' was sufficient protection, mirroring how other term-changing actions in this codebase are gated by lifecycle status alone.
correction: 'open' doesn't distinguish "nobody has acted on this yet" from "the market has already responded" — a Renter can currently edit a Requirement's commercial terms (capacity, dates, quantity, etc.) after one or more Rental Companies have already submitted a QuotationResponse against the original terms, or after an Auction has already been created against it, with no notification to the existing responder/participant that terms changed underneath them. This is the same class of gap CommercialQuotation.updateTerms and Rental.updateRentalTerms already close (both clear/restrict on a later-stage action) but RequirementService.updateRequirement does not. Documented in docs/backend-hardening-report.md rather than fixed — a product decision is needed on whether to block the edit once responded-to, or notify existing responders instead.
